On Aug 11, 2013, at 10:23 PM, Thomas, Neal wrote:
 
A few suggestions for compiler checks to project users
 

When a derived parameter is used in another formula before it is computed, diagnosing the problem is difficult. Is it possible to have the compiler check this condition?

If a parent parameter is typed in the model section (because we did not want to save it in the output), rstan crashes R in a hung state with no error message.  Can this be checked in the compile stage to avoid difficult to locate mistakes?

If variable typing does not match the constraints of the distribution of a parameter, confusing runtime errors can occur? Could consistent checks be built into the compiler?

Efficiency

Add vectorized 'pow' and scalar */+ vector/matrix definitions to increase ability to vectorize calculations

Rstan

rstan could have 'restart' for the 'fit' option to re-use more than the compiled code

rstan traceplot needs a 'window' option to allow more flexible starting location to exclude a few 'scale altering' starting values

More digits in default print

 


On Aug 3, 2013, at 2:14 PM, Thomas, Neal wrote:


I’ve had a chance to try out stan on about a dozen real examples with results that matter from the past 5 years.  The BUGS results have been re-produced every time (a good thing in a variety of ways).  Stan has converged faster with lower autocorrelation in every example I have tried.  Very impressive.  I have a few suggestions on things that could help users recover from their mistakes (I have made enough to be an expert on this) and suggest some mistakes to avoid regarding future funding that BUGS made.
